column1: # tools/ci-expected.tsv -- the allow-list `tools/ci-census.py` checks a build against.
# One row per allowed skip. Tab separated:
# not-run-total: 460
#   452 -> 455 on 2026-08-30 (ninth session): `flashwin` arrives at 13 with one
#   allowed skip covering 3. Its ten synthetic controls -- the rendering, the
#   endianness mutant, the publication guard in all three directions, the
#   half-open overlap boundary and its off-by-one mutant -- run anywhere; R1-R3
#   read this unit's own 4 MiB flash dump, which can never be committed. 量
#   2026-08-30 with $FWRE_WORK pointed at an empty directory: 10 ok / 0 FAIL /
#   1 skip line covering 3, which closes against 13.
#   UNCHANGED on 2026-08-30 (ninth session) although `test-console-capture`
#   grew 29 -> 40: every one of the eleven new cases drives a pty, and the
#   guard and metadata cases need no device, no vendor artefact and no
#   toolchain. So the suite adds 11 to the RUN total and 0 to this one.
#   Written down for the same reason the line below is: a session that changes
#   a suite and does not move this number looks exactly like a session that
#   forgot to.
#   UNCHANGED on 2026-08-29 (seventh session) although a suite arrived:
#   `check-predictions` is 6 cases, all of which run on a stock runner --
#   every fixture is a temporary directory the controls build themselves, and
#   nothing in it reads $FWRE_WORK, bench/ or a vendor artefact. So it adds 6
#   to the run total and 0 to this one. Written down because a session that
#   adds a suite and does not move this number looks exactly like a session
#   that forgot to.
#   `test-rtkimage` arrives at 32 with one allowed skip covering 18 (the GPL
#   drop), and `test-hazlint-objs` arrives at 28 and is *bench-only* for the
#   same reason `test-hazlint` is -- every one of its cases drives `hazlint`,
#   which refuses without `$FWRE_WORK/stage2.bin`. `test-deskchan` arrives at
#   18 and adds NOTHING here, because CI installs `qemu-system-mips` and the
#   suite then runs in full. ⚠️ This delta is arithmetic against the previous
#   measured value, not a fresh runner measurement: 量 2026-08-29 covers the
#   three new rows only (18 + 28 not run, checked with `--only`), and the 406
#   it is added to was measured on 2026-08-28/29.
#   The number ci-census prints as "NOT RUN IN THIS JOB", declared here so
#   that it is CHECKED rather than restated in a comment. 2026-08-29: the
#   green run of 2026-08-28 14:18 printed 373 while .github/workflows/ci.yml
#   said 362 -- wrong by 11, in the file whose own header spends forty lines
#   warning about a number that was true once. Nothing compared them.
#   373 -> 406 is test-hazlint 109 -> 142 (TC-j).
#   suite   bench_total   allowed_skip_label   covers   reason
# `bench_total` is the number of cases the suite prints WHEN EVERYTHING IT NEEDS
# IS PRESENT -- measured on the bench machine, not read off the source.
# `covers` is how many cases that one skip LINE stands for, and it is
# the field that matters: on a stock runner `tools/test-hazlint.sh` prints eight
# skip lines standing for twenty-five cases, and a census that counted lines
# would have reported eight.
# A suite with nothing to skip gets one row with `-` and 0.
# A suite CI does not run at all is marked `*bench-only*`, and its whole total
# counts as not run. It is listed rather than omitted because a suite nobody
# lists is a suite nobody misses.
# 2026-08-28 (fourth session): `kconfig-delta` (22), `mkinitramfs` (19) and
# `test-config-gates` (48, was 34) arrive with R3-4.  All three run on a clean clone --
# every control in the two tools is built on synthetic .config and declaration
# text, and the seven cases that are not are the E-block of test-config-gates,
# which reads the vendor template and this unit's own rootfs.  Read the note on
# `mkinitramfs` below: its A7 has no allowed skip on purpose.
# 2026-08-28: test-opcount 15 -> 24, test-hazlint 96 -> 109, and test-isa-probe
# arrives at 40. All three come out of `R2a/b/d-2`, and the one worth reading is
# hazlint's: the tool had been scanning a MIPS16 region four bytes at a time, so
# the cases added are a REFUSAL and its two mutations rather than more coverage of
# what it already did. test-isa-probe's A1 is the same shape one level up -- it
# asserts that a missing toolchain produces no table at all.
# 2026-08-27: test-hazlint 56 -> 96 and test-rlxprobe 195 -> 202, both from the
# COP3 correction in hazlint 1.2. Note what did NOT move: no violation count on
# any artefact in this tree changed, on either tool, before or after. The whole
# of the delta is controls and mutations -- which is the only way a fix that
# moves no number can be shown to have been a fix at all.
# 2026-08-26: spec-check went 10 -> 11 when it gained C8 and a ninth mutation.
# Caught by running ci-census against a fresh spec-check.out BEFORE the push --
# the second time a number in this repository would have been contradicted by
# the very next build (the first was ci.yml's own header, 2026-08-25).
# 2026-08-27 (second session): binsim arrives with two rows. `binsim` is the
# tool's own --self-test, twenty-three controls, none of which needs a vendor binary
# -- deliberately, because hazlint is *bench-only* for exactly the opposite
# reason and that means CI runs zero hazlint cases. `test-binsim` is 71 on the
# bench and 63 on a runner; the eight that stand down are the ones that read the
# six vendor trees. That eight was SEVEN when this row was first written, and
# the arithmetic here is what said so -- 48 + 7 = 55 against a bench total of 56,
# one short, because the section it stands for had eight cases and not seven.
# The suite was 56 then and is 65 now: `--fingerprint` turned out to have no case
# at all (seven added), and E0 -- the corpus's one-ISA membership rule -- got two
# more when a 2025 MediaTek image raised the question of a seventh tree; then 65 ->
# 71 when an adversarial review found three surviving mutants and a manifest no
# runner could reach.
# 2026-08-27 (third session), R2a/b/d-1: binsim 23 -> 24 and test-binsim 71 -> 96.
# The gate's step replaced the plan's refuted `@floor`, and the count is what
# that cost. Two things drive it.
# One: the real corpus stopped taking the REFUTED branch, and that branch had
# no fixture anywhere else -- a verdict that has stopped firing is not one that
# has been satisfied, it is one nobody is watching. So the verdict became a
# function (`floor_verdict`), `D5` drives it in both directions AND varies its
# second argument, `M11` inverts it, `M12` is the mutant that ignores CROSS
# entirely (an adversarial reviewer BUILT that one and it survived D5's first
# version), and `X` builds a second synthetic corpus that lands on the refuted
# side.
# Two: the step's first answer was wrong and the review caught it. `@floor` had
# been moved to `busybox unit-2018/v3.4.0` = 0.1646, which clears CROSS 0.1581
# -- but containment divides by the SMALLER feature set, and busybox's is 1.46x
# boa's, so the two numbers were read at different denominators. At a matched
# denominator the ordering reverses. The floor is now the CROSS cell itself in
# the new five-field cross-program form, `E7` asserts it is the top of a
# three-program population at ONE denominator, and `E8` measures what a
# compilation-model change alone costs (`@model`, pppd 2.4.4 in two trees).
# The corpus gained three `baseline` rows for that: 18 -> 21.
# The R section went 8 -> 22, and the shape of the new fourteen is the point:
# two read the PREMISE of the floor choice rather than its consequence (one
# BusyBox version and one boa version across all six trees), two pin that BASE
# and FLOOR share a denominator, three pin the population E7 takes a maximum
# over, two pin E8's reading, and two sweep the named cell's rank over k in
# both directions -- it is overtaken at k=1, which is what makes the other five
# rows mean something.
# suite

column1: spec-check
column5: 11 -> 23 on 2026-08-30 (tenth session). C8 stopped being about SPEC.md: it now runs over every tracked `.md` outside `upstream/` -- 71 files, 620 tables, ~3,600 rows, ~43,000 code spans -- because how this repository's prose renders is not a property of one file. 量 the first time it ran that way: EIGHT ragged rows against a census that had said six, because that census had looked at three files. Three more shapes came with it, each found by turning the previous one on: C8b a row split over more than one PHYSICAL line (two instances, and one of them blinded every checker here to the rest of its table), C8c a `|`-line belonging to NO table (NINE rows of docs/FINDINGS.md -- the page a reader is pointed at, including the three newest findings -- plus one of bench/README.md; C8 cannot see this by construction, since C8 walks tables and a stranded row is in none), and C9 a code span whose whole content is whitespace (FOUR instances, one of which made a READING wrong rather than a rendering: docs/loader-command-semantics.md annotated BOTH exits of readline's three-way branch with the same empty character; the fourth is the carried-forward row that DESCRIBES the defect, and only running the finished checker over `git archive HEAD` found it -- the count assembled one file at a time said three). Whole reading over the tree at HEAD: C8 8, C8b 2, C8c 10, C9 4 -- 24 defects in six files. The twelve new case lines are ten fixture controls plus their summary and the sweep's own report. T1 is the POSITIVE one and is why the rest mean anything -- a checker that fires on everything passes every mutation; T5 is a control on that control (with the fence mask off, the clean fixture must go red); T7 refuses on a population that is empty, has no SPEC.md, or descends into upstream/. The fixture is built in the process, not committed, so all twelve run anywhere git does 🔄 23 -> 30 on 2026-08-30 (twelfth session, after the seating). `C10` is new: a paragraph whose backtick RUNS cannot pair, so a code span is left open and swallows the prose after it. It exists because `C9` pairs runs across the WHOLE FILE, which makes an unmatched run invisible until later text happens to supply a partner -- order dependent, and 量 that is what hid three of these. One had been committed for a day with every other check passing over it: `notes/kernel-build.md` rendered a whole sentence as code while `0x2B0000`, the number the sentence is about, rendered as prose; `RUNSHEET.md` closed a span with a run of TWO, which leaves the backtick COUNT even so a parity test misses it. Seven new case lines: T11 (an opening run that never closes), T14 (the doubled closer -- run LENGTH against backtick COUNT, the shape a parity implementation passes T11 and misses), T15 (two paragraphs with one unclosed run each, which pins the PARAGRAPH boundary: an implementation pairing file-wide reports none), T12 (the negative -- a paragraph whose runs pair is clean), T13 (a control on the EXEMPTION: the one frozen prediction block that cannot be repaired must still fire without its entry, so a repaired file forces the entry out instead of hiding a later defect), T16 (a file with no trailing newline -- every other control appends text ending in one, so the trailing yield was never exercised) and T17 (the finding names the paragraph's first line, COMPUTED from the fixture rather than hardcoded). 🔴 T14, T16 and T17 exist because `tools/test-spec-check-mutants.py` ran twelve mutants against the first version and THREE survived. All seven run on the built-in fixture, so this adds 7 to the run total and 0 to `not-run-total`

column1: test-console-capture
column5: 29 -> 40 on 2026-08-30 with the terminator guard and the two metadata fields (R3-9). Eleven cases, of which **seven are controls** under this file's own definition (a case whose id begins `N` — the tool must refuse, or a mutant must break a case above); the suite's header count moves 17 → 24 by exactly those seven: N18/N20 (the refusal, and that an explicit `--seconds 0 --idle 0` is the same request in longhand), N19 (it fires before the port is opened -- the ordering _check_send exists for), N21 (the sandwich: a 127-char --send with no terminator must hit the TERMINATOR refusal, which proves the guard sits after the length check and before the port, from one command), N22 (both metadata fields move with their arguments, so they are recorded rather than constant), N23 and N24 (the two mutations -- guard dead, fields hardcoded). P13 is not a duplicate of P12: a guard written on --seconds alone passes P12 and refuses every --idle capture, including RUNSHEET D1, whose measured quantity IS a silence. 🔴 P4 CHANGED rather than being added to: it now passes --seconds 1, because its assertion is that a 127-character line REACHES the port, and 量 2026-08-30 it is the only one of this file's four terminator-less invocations that the guard reaches -- N4, N7 and N8 are refused inside _check_send first. All eleven run on a stock runner (a pty, no device), so this row adds 11 to the run total and 0 to `not-run-total`. 🔄 That total is **455**, not the 452 this sentence said when it was written: `flashwin` arrived in the same session and moved it by 3. A row that names the total it does not change still has to name it correctly 🔄 40 -> 46 the same day, and the reason is the only kind that counts: tools/test-console-capture-mutants.py ran 25 mutants of the terminator guard against those forty cases and TEN survived. They fell into four classes and not one of the forty could see a class rather than an instance. N25/N26 close WAIVER (an early `return` on any flag the cases leave at default -- `if args.esc > 0: return` passed all forty, and `--esc 25` is A-catch's own shape; 量 on a pty that mutant gives rc=124 with the .meta.json lost). N27 closes CONTRACT, both halves in one case: no case asserted an exit code, so `SystemExit(0)` was green and a card written `cmd || abort` would read a refusal as success; and none looked at stdout, so a refusal printed there was green too. N28 closes MESSAGE (one substring passed a refusal naming `--timeout`, a flag that does not exist). N29/N30 close POSITION, which N21 only appeared to cover: N21 sends 127 characters, a line _check_send ACCEPTS, so it passes whether or not the guard sits above it -- N29 sends 128 and requires the LENGTH refusal, and N30 pre-creates the output files and requires the TERMINATOR refusal ahead of the overwrite one. All six drive --port /dev/null and add 0 to not-run-total

column1: test-console-capture-mutants
column5: arrives 2026-08-30 (tenth session), and it exists because test-console-capture reported 40/40 while TEN mutations of the guard it had just gained were alive. "Nine survived" had been a sentence in LOG.md that nothing re-ran; this is what makes it a number that can go red. Same shape as test-rbcheck.py. Each row edits console-capture.py at anchors that must occur EXACTLY ONCE -- a moved anchor is reported as a SURVIVOR, never skipped -- and requires the WHOLE of test-console-capture.sh to go red against the result; a proxy for the suite would be a different claim. The 25 are 8 WAIVER, 5 CONDITION, 3 POSITION (a move is two edits, so writing it as one would be a delete), 3 CONTRACT/MESSAGE, 4 METADATA, and 2 on _check_send itself -- those last two are there because if either survives, the guard's cases are covering for _check_send's and P1 is being killed by luck. It refuses outright if the unmutated suite is not green, since every mutation would then "kill" on a suite that was already red. Mutants run 8 at a time because the cases are sleep-bound (ptys and played gaps), not CPU-bound: 量 on this host, 336 s wall for 24 against an 84 s baseline. Needs a pty and python3-serial and nothing else -- no device, no $FWRE_WORK -- so all 25 run here and add 0 to not-run-total

column1: test-spec-check-mutants
column5: arrives 2026-08-30 (twelfth session) and it exists for the reason `test-console-capture-mutants` proved two days earlier: a green control suite is a claim about the suite. `spec-check` gained `C10` and reported all fifteen table controls green; twelve mutants of `C10` and its two helpers were run against those controls and **three survived** -- the final paragraph never being yielded (invisible because every control appended text ending in a newline), fenced blocks scanned as prose (invisible because the fixture's fences all paired), and the reported line number off by one (nothing asserted it). T16, T17 and a new fixture fence closed all three; 12/12 now. Each row edits `tools/spec-check.py` at anchors that must occur EXACTLY ONCE -- a moved anchor is reported as a SURVIVOR, never skipped -- and requires the WHOLE `--self-test` (nine SPEC.md controls plus seventeen table controls) to go red. 🔴 The harness is the awkward part and it is measured rather than assumed: `spec-check.py` computes ROOT from its own path, so a mutant cannot be run from /tmp. Each one gets a temp root of symlinks to every top-level repository entry (including `.git`, so `git ls-files` still answers, which T7 requires) plus a `tools/` of symlinked siblings and the mutant as a real file; 量, a clean copy through that harness exits 0 and a C10-never-fires mutant exits 2, which is what says the harness is wired up at all. Twelve mutant lines plus the summary = 13 cases, all of them synthetic -- no device, no $FWRE_WORK, no pty -- so this 🔴 13 -> 18 the same evening, and the reason is the one that matters: an adversarial pass found that `main()` returns on `--self-test` **before `check_tables()` is ever called**, and `table_controls` calls the finding functions directly — so **no mutation in `check_tables` or `report_tables` could be killed by this suite's criterion, by construction**. Seven hand-written mutants passed all three CI gates, two of them disabling `C10` repository-wide while every gate stayed green. **Phase 2** plants three real `C10` defects — prose with a shifting pairing, a table row, and a run of three — in a **tracked** file inside the temp root (`bench/README.md`, under `bench/` so a path-prefix exemption is also caught) and runs the **full** tool, requiring the mutant to report **fewer** than the baseline's three. Counting rather than testing for presence is what makes suppressing one of three visible: `P4` and `P5` each suppress exactly one. Phase 2 carries its own positive control — the unmutated tool must report all three, or every row would 'kill' a run that never saw the defect. `P1`/`P2` are the two that were invisible before. ⚠️ Two rows had to be remodelled on the way: `P2`'s anchor occurred twice and `P5`'s mutation stepped past the first backtick of a three-run so the run became a two-run and the defect still fired — the label said "not counted" and the edit said "counted shorter". Both were reported as SURVIVOR rather than skipped, which is the design. adds 18 to the run total and 0 to `not-run-total`

column1: leakscan
column5: arrives 2026-08-30 (thirteenth session) and is rebuilt the day after (fourteenth). It exists because the whole of this repository's leak checking was ONE CI step over `bench/**/*.log` -- 240 files out of the 898 `git ls-files` returns (899 lines, one of them the submodule gitlink). 量: the 658 tracked files it never reads, plus `upstream/`'s 302 that `git ls-files` cannot see at all -- 960 unread -- and it imports audit-bench-log.py's PATTERNS/ALLOW rather than copying them (TC-j) and NEVER PRINTS WHAT MATCHED. 🔄 6 -> 16 on 2026-08-30 (fourteenth session), and the ten new controls exist because the FIRST day's finding was wrong in every clause: it reported one MAC on `FC:19:28`, called that TOTOLINK's OUI, and recorded the attribution as undetermined because FW-17's SSID correlation could not be run. 量: `FC:19:28` is Actions Microelectronics (IEEE MA-L, 2020-08-25); the value equals the `enx<12hex>` interface name in nine tracked files, is the source of the echo REPLIES in both committed host captures and never of the requests, and occurs 0 times in this unit's own 4 MiB dump -- it is the WORKSTATION's USB GbE adapter and never was the device's. The correlation that could not be run was never the only one available: the dump is the arbiter and it was on the disk the whole time. `--attribute` replaces the prefix guess with that lookup and L7-L14 are its controls, every one on a synthetic 4 MiB-shaped fixture so they run on a runner. L9 is the one the never-print property actually needed -- a throwaway probe written the same day printed a 3-byte OUI into a transcript because its masking covered the file lines it echoed and not the lookup strings it built, and L9 asserts a rendered attribution contains the value in NONE of seven encodings and not the OUI either. L13 pins the ORDER: a measurement (these bytes are in this unit's flash) beats every inference above it (locally administered; a scanner's own literal). L15 reads THIS TABLE and asserts the label below is the label the tool prints -- the fix test-kbuild-cflags needed after CI run 33310864156, because a machine with $FWRE_WORK never prints the skip and so never compares it. 🔴 Only `--self-test` is in CI. The verdict run needs the real dump, and the allowlist it would need is deliberately NOT taken: the device is end of life and the owner's decision on the one UNIT finding is recorded in SPEC.md §18 as a decision rather than as an oversight. 🔄 16 -> 17 the same evening: L17 drives the real path text -> abl.scan -> scan_population -> mac_bytes, because every other control hands `classify` a byte string directly and a decoder that dropped one of the four MAC encodings would make every hit in that form NOVALUE -- classified, counted, and silently never looked up. 16 of the 17 run anywhere git does: 16 to the run total, 1 to not-run-total

column1: test-leakscan-mutants
column5: arrives 2026-08-30 (fourteenth session). It exists because `leakscan.py`'s `main()` RETURNS on `--self-test` before the reporting loop runs, so no control in that suite can reach `populations()`'s use site, the IDENTITY filter in the report, or the per-population totals -- which is exactly where the mutant PROGRESS.md had named lives ("the population filter widened so upstream/ is dropped, which would turn 52 findings into a silent 0"). Same structural hole, and same answer, as test-spec-check-mutants.py. THREE phases: phase 1 mutates the classifier and requires `--self-test` to go red; phase 2 runs the WHOLE tool over a planted synthetic corpus of eight known hits and requires the report's SIGNATURE to change -- per-population triples, per-file line counts and the two summary numbers, because a count of planted lines alone left three mutants alive; phase 3 runs `--attribute` over a corpus planted with a value read OUT OF THE DUMP AT RUNTIME plus a DECOY carrying the same three-byte OUI and a different tail, and requires the tool's stdout to contain the value in none of four encodings. 🔴 The decoy is the original defect in one line: a classifier that matches on the vendor prefix -- which is what audit-bench-log.py's `MAC, bare 12 hex` pattern does -- calls it the device's, and one that requires the whole address does not. 量 2026-08-30: the FIRST run had EIGHT survivors. Three were defects in the mutants themselves (two written against a function the value is not even in scope of; one whose anchor occurred twice and was correctly reported NOT APPLIED rather than skipped). Five were real: a `render` printing the whole finding tuple, bytes included, past a control that checked two string forms of the value and not its repr; and four criteria too coarse to see a changed report. 23/23 killed now. 20 run anywhere git does; A1-A3 need $FWRE_WORK/dumps/flash-n150rt-console-2.bin and are skipped as one line covering 3 23 -> 24 the same evening: Q1 asserts THIS TABLE's allowed-skip column equals the label the suite prints. The owner audit caught this file adding an unchecked label in the very session whose write-up counts how many suites check theirs -- the label is now one variable used three times, and Q1 runs in BOTH configurations because a machine with the dump prints no skip and so compares nothing. It needs no vendor material: 21 of the 24 run anywhere git does

column1: test-kbuild-cflags
column3: C1 the declared flags reach the build
column5: arrives 2026-08-30 (thirteenth session). `rlxfw-kbuild.sh` had no suite at all, and the thing it now guards is the one that turned out to matter: 量, the image that BOOTED could not be rebuilt from its own recorded configuration because `-fno-if-conversion` (TC-25, seven load-use violations to zero) lived only in the operator's shell. FOUR of the five cases need no vendor material, and that is a property of WHERE the guard sits rather than luck: it runs above the stage and above the drop check, so a refusal costs no 480 MB copy -- a refusal nobody can afford to exercise is one nobody exercises. C2 is the case the first version of the guard failed (`--cflags-kernel ""` fell through to the declared file, which is the one request the file exists to refuse -- console-capture's N20 is the same distinction one tool over). C6 is the control on the other three: `--no-cflags` must be ACCEPTED and must NOT read the declaration, or a guard that refuses everything would pass C2/C4/C5. The last case asserts the declaration file's sha256 is unchanged, because C4 and C5 move and rewrite it -- and its first version grepped for a string the file's own comment block also contains and reported 2. 🔴 9 -> 10 the same evening: CI went red on `UNEXPECTED-SKIP 'C1 the declared flags reach the build'` while this suite was 9/9 green on the bench. `ci-census` counts a skip only when its printed label appears in this column, and the column said `C1 the GPL drop` -- a label the suite never prints. 🔴 THE BENCH CANNOT SEE THAT CLASS: on the machine the push happens from, `$FWRE_WORK` holds the GPL drop, so C1 RUNS, no skip line is printed, and no label is ever compared. `C7` is the new case and it reads THIS FILE, which is the only check that works in both configurations; C1's label is now a shell variable used for the case, the skip and the assertion, so the two spellings cannot drift again. C1 stages a tree and stands down without a drop: 9 ok / 0 FAIL / 1 skip covering 1, which closes against 10. Adds 10 to the run total and 1 to not-run-total, which is unchanged at 456

column1: verify-backup-copy
ci-census
column5: 19 -> 21 on 2026-08-30 (thirteenth session). C16, both directions: the not-run-total check must NOT fire under --only and must still fire without it. It exists because CLAUDE.md own pre-push step is --only <the suites you touched>, and on the machine the push happens from -- which has FWRE_WORK and therefore runs everything -- that command could never go green, since not-run-total describes a RUNNER. A documented procedure that cannot pass is one nobody follows. Both halves are asserted because a fix that disabled the check outright would pass the first alone. Synthetic: 2 to the run total, 0 to not-run-total

column1: test-opcount
column5: needs binutils-mips-linux-gnu; CI installs it, so this skip should NOT appear. 15 -> 24 -> 29 on 2026-08-28 (the last five out of the adversarial review: P6/P7/P9 pin that the control-did-not-fire guard covers BOTH verdicts and not just the zero, and P8 pins the codeness filter with a data island -- three mutants that passed the 24-case suite all die on the 29): P2/N3/N4 for --pairs, the unaligned-access idiom rather than the bare opcode, and P3-P5 for --mips16, the precondition the docstring's superset claim turned out to need

column1: test-isa-probe
column5: needs a vendor toolchain: the rsdk assemblers ship inside the GPL drops under $FWRE_WORK/rebuild/src-vendor and are not in a clone. column1: flashwin
column5: 🔄 13 -> 19 the same day, after an adversarial pass ran 45 mutants against the first self-test and **24 survived** -- three of them printed this unit's MAC (the rendering written to stdout on the refusal path, the withheld digest printed beside the word `withheld`, and the dump never opened at all). The common cause: every case that could leak used ONE argument triple against an ALL-ZERO dump, and R1/R2 called `render_dw()` in process, so nothing between `open the file` and `format the words` had a control over it. Rewritten: every leak-capable case drives the real command line as a subprocess and asserts stdout is EMPTY, R1/R2 go through `--out` + `cmp`, and the synthetic dump is no longer all zeros. 22 of 22 of the surviving mutants are now killed. R1 and R2 render bench/2026-08-24d/G8a-rd0.log and G8a-rd6.log out of $FWRE_WORK/dumps/flash-n150rt-console-2.bin and require them byte for byte; R3 requires the two 2026-08-16 dumps to be identical over all 4,194,304 bytes. A 4 MiB image of this unit's own flash can never be committed, so the three stand down on a runner. The TEN that run anywhere are the ones that make the skip a skip: C1-C5 pin the rendering and its endianness against a mutant, C6/C7/C8 drive the publication guard as a SUBPROCESS in all three directions (no --out refuses, --out inside the repository refuses and writes nothing, --out outside is accepted and prints no digest), and C9/C10 pin the half-open overlap test at both ends with the off-by-one mutant that would let a straddling window through. 量 2026-08-30 with $FWRE_WORK pointed at an empty directory: 16 ok / 0 FAIL / 1 skip line covering 3, which closes against 19. 🔴 This sentence read "10 ok ... closes against 13" until the tenth session -- both halves were the PRE-rewrite numbers, left in the row whose whole job is to carry the number, while the gate column beside them already said 19 🔄 19 -> 24 on 2026-08-30 (fourteenth session): the `normalise` subcommand and its five controls. A `DW` reply carries the typed command and a `%08X:` address column, both holding the RAM DESTINATION, so two reads of the SAME flash window into DIFFERENT RAM addresses do not `cmp` equal -- which is why the bracket's second half had to reuse the first half's destination, and reusing it costs a control: with one destination, "the RAM already held these bytes" is not excluded and an FLR that did nothing looks like one that worked. N2 is the case that matters (the same window rendered at 0x80B50000 normalises identically to the capture taken at 0x80A00000) and N3 is its control (two different windows do not). N5 refuses a file that is not a DW reply, with nothing on stdout. All five read the two committed 777-byte captures and no dump, so they add 5 to the run total and 0 to not-run-total 24 -> 27 the same evening, and the three new controls came from an adversarial pass rather than from thought: eight mutants of `normalise` against N1-N5 and THREE survived -- a garbage data line under a valid echo (N6), a reply with no data lines at all (N7), and a normaliser that SORTED the words, which would make two windows with the same multiset compare equal and which N3 structurally could not see because its two windows differ in content as well as in order (N8). 🔴 The pass itself had to be re-run: the first attempt reported 8 of 8 killed with every one "killed by C7b,C7c", and 量 the UNMUTATED file through that same symlinked temp root was already 22/24 -- C7b/C7c resolve the repository root with realpath, which a symlink farm sends back to the real tree, so every kill was invalid. The baseline-through-the-harness control that test-spec-check-mutants.py has is exactly what it was missing. All three new controls build their fixture in a temp dir and read no dump: 24 of the 27 run anywhere git does
